description:
We are a team of students from Ukraine who enjoy turning ideas into working projects. Our interests include space exploration, programming, engineering, 3D modelling, and design.

We are developing ARES-7, an interactive survival game where players manage a space station, solve technical problems, and make decisions to keep the crew alive.

We bring curiosity, hands-on STEM experience, and a willingness to learn together.
summary:
**ARES-7** is an interactive educational Mars survival simulator where players take on the role of a team of astronauts responsible for building and maintaining a sustainable Martian base.
We developed a game that simulates real challenges of future space missions, including energy generation, oxygen and water production, food cultivation, habitat protection, local resource utilization, and overall station management.
The key feature of ARES-7 is its interconnected decision-making system. Every action affects the station's resources, operating conditions, and crew safety. Poor decisions have consequences, while successful survival requires critical thinking, strategic planning, and balancing competing priorities.

Our project addresses the lack of practical, hands-on learning opportunities in space exploration and STEM education. Instead of simply memorizing scientific facts, students learn through experimentation, problem-solving, and experiencing the consequences of their decisions.
**ARES-7 transforms complex scientific concepts into an engaging, interactive learning experience**, helping students develop engineering skills, critical thinking, and an understanding of sustainable resource management.
The simulator can be used in classrooms and educational activities, even without a constant internet connection.
details:
ARES-7: Survive, Explore, and Learn on Mars

Project Overview

ARES-7 is an interactive educational survival and management simulator that challenges players to operate a damaged research station on Mars. The project combines space exploration, engineering, environmental science, resource management, and strategic decision-making in a single learning experience.

Our goal was to make complex challenges of space exploration understandable and engaging for students. Instead of simply reading about the technologies needed for human survival on Mars, players can experiment with them, make decisions, experience consequences, and learn from their mistakes.

How Does ARES-7 Work?

Players take control of a Martian research station experiencing technical failures and limited resources. Their primary objective is to restore critical systems, transmit a distress signal, and keep the crew alive throughout a 20-day survival mission.

The station contains several interconnected systems:

  • Energy Management: Generate and distribute electricity while balancing consumption and available reserves.
  • Life Support: Maintain oxygen supplies, manage air filtration, and support safe living conditions.
  • Food Production: Operate a greenhouse, grow crops, and manage water, lighting, and nutrients.
  • Habitat Protection: Repair damaged structures and respond to environmental hazards.
  • Resource Extraction: Explore the Martian environment, identify valuable materials, and manage extraction risks.
  • Mission Control: Coordinate station operations, prioritize repairs, respond to emergencies, and complete exploration missions.

Every decision affects the station's condition. For example, increasing energy consumption may help restore oxygen production but reduce the electricity available for other critical systems. Using too much water in the greenhouse can threaten the crew's drinking water supply.

Players must therefore consider not only the immediate benefits of an action but also its long-term consequences.

Educational Features and Innovation

One of the most important features of ARES-7 is its decision-making and feedback system.

The game does not assume that every player will make the correct decision. Instead, it introduces mistakes, emergencies, limited resources, and competing priorities.

A scoring system records positive and negative outcomes, explains the reasons behind them, and helps players understand how their decisions influence the mission.

ARES-7 also includes interactive educational challenges, such as repairing electrical circuits, balancing life-support systems, extracting resources, and navigating exploration missions.

An interactive station map allows players to explore different modules and understand how their functions are connected.

The integrated Training Center provides scientific explanations and references to NASA educational resources. Scientific principles are adapted into simplified models suitable for learning rather than presented as exact engineering simulations.

Technologies and Development Tools

ARES-7 was developed primarily using accessible web technologies:

  • HTML5: Structure of the game interface and interactive elements.
  • CSS3: Visual design, responsive layouts, and the Martian station environment.
  • JavaScript: Simulation logic, resource calculations, event handling, interactive missions, scoring, and minigames.
  • Python and Flask: Tools used during local development and testing.
  • GitHub and GitHub Pages: Source-code hosting and web deployment.

The project also uses browser-based storage for certain settings and does not require specialized hardware.

A self-contained HTML version allows the simulator to run locally without a constant internet connection, making it suitable for classrooms with limited connectivity.

Creativity and Advantages

The creativity of ARES-7 lies in combining several engineering and scientific challenges into one interconnected simulation.

Rather than presenting independent educational quizzes, the game creates a virtual environment where the consequences of decisions influence future opportunities.

Its main advantages include accessibility, interactive learning, immediate feedback, multiple gameplay activities, and the possibility of learning through failure without real-world risks.

The project is designed to encourage students to think like engineers: analyze problems, identify constraints, compare alternatives, test solutions, and improve their strategies.

Expected Impact

ARES-7 aims to increase students' interest in STEM education, space exploration, and sustainable technologies.

By managing a simulated Martian station, players can develop critical thinking, systems thinking, problem-solving skills, and a better understanding of resource conservation.

The project can be used in schools, STEM clubs, science events, and independent learning activities.

Although the game focuses on Mars, many of its educational concepts are relevant to Earth, including efficient energy use, water conservation, sustainable food production, and emergency preparedness.

Factors Considered by Our Team

During development, our team considered several important factors: scientific credibility, educational value, accessibility, gameplay balance, technical simplicity, and user engagement.

We wanted to create a game that would be challenging enough to encourage thoughtful decisions while remaining understandable to students without advanced engineering knowledge.

We also considered limited internet access, the need for clear instructions, realistic consequences of mistakes, and the importance of explaining how and why the simulation calculates outcomes.

Our vision is to transform space exploration from something students only read about into something they can experience, investigate, and understand through their own decisions.

ARES-7 is more than a survival game. It is an educational environment where every resource matters, every decision has consequences, and every mistake can become an opportunity to learn.
